title: Don’t Want Explosive Diarrhea? Shop Local and Regulate Big Ag
author: Sonali Kolhatkar
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/Screenshot-2026-07-30-at-1.22.03-PM-680x520.png)

Photo by [Jef
Wright](https://unsplash.com/@thejefwright?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText)

The recent, record-breaking outbreak of Cyclospora infections linked to
[lettuce consumption](https://www.washingtonpost.com/health/2026/07/21/can-i-
eat-lettuce-now-what-know-about-cyclosporiasis-outbreak/) has left Americans
wondering what food is safe to eat.

What brands of lettuce are safe and which aren’t are important questions. But
even more important might be why such outbreaks happen in the first place —
and how our government has made them [increasingly
likely](https://www.cdc.gov/foodnet/reports/preliminary-data.html).

Nobody wants explosive diarrhea — and yet the way our federal government has
left us unprotected is enough to make one sick.

The chief culprit in the cyclosporiasis debacle is our centralized, monopoly-
based food system. The outbreak has been [linked to Taylor Fresh
Foods](https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5992816-lettuce-outbreak-white-
house-influence/), which supplies many restaurants. [Many brands of bagged
lettuce and salad are also Taylor
products](https://wisemomblogger.com/10-proven-brands-that-get-their-lettuce-
from-taylor-farms/) — whether consumers realize it or not.

In fact, according to [Farm Action](https://farmaction.us/if-it-isnt-taylor-
farms-then-who/), “Just four companies — Taylor Fresh Foods, Cultrale-Safra,
Itochu, and Bonduelle — control 54 percent of the U.S. fresh-cut salad
market.” Similarly, only a [handful of
corporations](https://primesourcex.com/who-controls-your-food-the-rise-of-
monopolies-in-the-u-s-food-industry/) control meat, dairy, grains, and
beverages. Another [handful controls food
distribution](https://thecapitolforum.com/war-in-the-aisles-monopolies-across-
the-grocery-supply-chain/).

This means that the industry practices giving rise to contaminated foods
happen on a very large scale — and those foods are then distributed all over
the country. That a single outbreak in one company can [potentially impact the
entire nation](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/27/cyclospora-outbreak-food-
industry-consolidation.html) is a grave weakness in the food system.

Monopolies like Taylor Farms use the profits they generate from dominating our
food supplies to lobby the federal government for weaker oversight. According
to [ _Wired_](https://www.wired.com/story/diarrhea-outbreak-taylor-farms-maga-
donations-lobbying/), the company has contributed millions of dollars to
conservative political committees, including a super PAC called MAGA Inc.

It has also spent hundreds of thousands of dollars to directly lobby against
food safety regulations. [News even
emerged](https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5992816-lettuce-outbreak-white-
house-influence/) recently of representatives from Taylor Farms calling the
White House to try to delay a recall of their lettuce.

The Trump administration has been more than happy to comply with Big Food’s
wishes to reap billions in profits with little oversight.

Last year the administration [weakened](https://cepr.net/publications/how-
donald-trump-made-it-easier-for-you-to-get-diarrhea/) the nation’s already
thin food safety monitoring service,
[FoodNet](https://www.cdc.gov/foodnet/index.html), by making it [optional to
track numerous types of infections](https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-
news/cdc-quietly-scaled-back-surveillance-program-foodborne-illnesses-
rcna227089) —  _including cyclosporiasis_. “We’re really gutting one of the
cornerstones of food safety,” epidemiologist Elaine Scallan Walter warned the
[ _New York Times_](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/10/well/cdc-foodnet.html)
last September.

Mega monopolies aren’t just bad for our gut. They also contribute to higher
prices and reduced access to fresh foods.

Their sheer size gives them what [Civil
Eats](https://civileats.com/2021/02/17/op-ed-monopolies-in-the-food-system-
make-food-more-expensive-and-less-accessible/) called “enormous power to make
decisions about what food is produced how, where, and by whom, and who gets to
eat it.” Big Food companies have repeatedly been found guilty of illegal price
fixing. They routinely package the same foods under different labels to give
the impression of diversity and competition.

Small farms are one important solution. Their supply chains are localized,
making it easier to track and stop infections before they spread on a national
scale. Independent farmers are [selling
out](https://www.fox10tv.com/2026/07/15/lettuce-sells-out-farmers-market-amid-
concerns-over-explosive-diarrhea-outbreak/) of lettuce at farmers markets as
people seek out clean greens.

Yet instead of promoting and aiding small farmers — as he
[promised](https://www.ap.org/news-highlights/elections/2024/trump-listens-
during-a-farming-event-in-rural-pennsylvania-then-threatens-john-deere-with-
tariffs/) to do when running for president in 2024 — President Trump has [cut
back support](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jul/11/iowa-farming-
trump-cuts-usda) for training new farmers, who might be competitors to
companies like Taylor Farms.

His administration [also cut a
program](https://www.kqed.org/news/12088977/a-lifeline-for-californias-small-
farms-just-expired-what-comes-next) that matched small producers with food
banks — feeding hungry people while financially stabilizing independent
farmers — along with a [disaster aid
program](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2024/06/10/usda-minority-
farmers-injunction/) for minority farmers. The funding losses have left small
farmers [reeling](https://civileats.com/2026/06/01/losing-ground-how-trump-is-
setting-back-local-food-and-small-farms/).

What will help prevent future outbreaks is restoring and expanding regulatory
agencies tracking infectious outbreaks. And breaking up food monopolies while
sustaining and strengthening small farms.

The question is: will the federal government have the guts to do what it takes
to protect the American people’s guts?
